sources.title: Handley Page Halifax JB798 (WMR-30919)
sources.summary: IWM entry for a metal plaque on the wall in the south west corner of the nave of St James Church, Selby. It records the 1944 spire strike and the church's restoration and re-dedication, and says the plaque is shown with British and Australian flags and the spire's golden cockerel. It names no maintainer.

paragraphs.text: The aeroplane that struck the spire of St James Church, Selby, on 10 May 1944 was Halifax JB789 of 1658 Heavy Conversion Unit, Riccall, not JB798. The IWM register lists this plaque under the serial JB798.

The plaque is on the nave wall at St James Church, Selby, and is shown with British and Australian flags and the spire's cockerel. The church was restored from 10 May 1949 and re-dedicated on 11 December 1950. Yorkshire Aircraft says a memorial plaque was unveiled in the church on 1 November 1953.

notes: DUPLICATE VERDICT: SAME memorial and same aircraft. Correct serial is JB789 (1658 HCU, Riccall). (1) Yorkshire Aircraft traces JB789 from 158 Sqn to 1658 HCU and the 10 May 1944 Selby spire strike (two pages). (2) IWM 30919, titled JB798, describes one plaque in St James Church recording a 10 May 1944 RAF aeroplane striking the spire; no source shows a second Selby memorial or a second Halifax. (3) JB798 was a different airframe: IBCC puts JB798 (78 Sqn, EY-P, Fraser) on the Hamburg raid of 30 July 1943, crashed at Bad Oldesloe, crew buried Hamburg. The seven crew names in our JB798 record (Fraser, Nicholls, Hetherington, Baillie, Goodacre, Campbell, Woodcock) are that 1943 crew, not the Selby crew; IWM's inscription text as we hold it appears to carry them too. The Selby crew per Yorkshire Aircraft are Laver, McDermott, Rockingham, Storer, Knight, Roper, Dixon. Caveat: coordinates differ by about 200 m (53.784012,-1.068781 vs 53.782467,-1.071457; the IWM grid SE 61280 32193 is the plaque position); both are inside the one church area, and the 1953 plaque date (Yorkshire Aircraft) vs a plaque mentioning 1950 re-dedication (IWM) could mean two plaques, not checked. Our JB789 record's 9 May 1944 date is unsupported: both IWM and Yorkshire Aircraft say 10 May. Recommend merging the JB798 record into JB789 after human review. CUSTODIAN: not found; same findings as selby-halifax-jb789 (IWM names no maintainer; church sites silent). CREW DOUBT: the seven crew in this record are the 78 Sqn JB798 crew lost over Hamburg on 30 July 1943 per IBCC (S3), not the Selby aircrew; crew names are not retracted here, flagged for human decision. The 'civilian parishioners' list in the IWM inscription as held also repeats those names, so the inscription text should be re-checked against the IWM page photographs. Not covered: the record's memorial_details and inscription fields were left alone; the record title/serial would need correcting if merged.
